newsitem.title: USA: Morocco sorghum tax change could trigger US sales.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sorghum tax change could trigger US sales.

text.p: Morocco's recent decision to lower its value-added tax on U.S. sorghum imports could quickly lead to sales, the U.S. Feed Grains Council said Thursday.

"This is really exciting news," USFGC President Ken Hobbe said in a prepared statement. "Just last year, most Moroccan poultry and livestock producers, due to government constraints, had never even seen sorghum."
Over the past two years, the USFGC has conducted a series of feeding trials in Morocco using U.S. sorghum donated by the Kansas Grain Sorghum Commission.
Those efforts recently paid off when Morocco reduced its value-added tax on sorghum to seven percent from 20 percent, the same as for corn.
The change has made the price of U.S. sorghum "very attractive to (Moroccan) buyers and sales could begin very soon," the council said.
